taxonomy.kew_note: Kew accepts the subspecies; Argemone albiflora var. texana is treated as a synonym.

project_inclusion.regional_note: Documented in Central Texas, including Williamson County; native to Texas.

morphology_keys.habit: Robust, erect, spiny herb; stems sparsely to moderately prickly.
morphology_keys.foliage: Conspicuously glaucous; basal/proximal leaves deeply lobed nearly to the midrib.
morphology_keys.leaf_prickles: Upper surface often unarmed or only sparsely prickly; lower surface prickly especially along major veins.
morphology_keys.latex: Light to pale yellow when fresh.
morphology_keys.flower: Large white flower; petals white; numerous lemon-yellow stamens.
morphology_keys.bud_sepals: Sepal horns about 4–6(-10) mm; typically unarmed or only sparingly prickly near the base.
morphology_keys.capsule: Usually narrowly ellipsoid; longer prickles widely spaced and mixed with numerous shorter unequal prickles; longest prickles much shorter than in A. aurantiaca.
morphology_keys.flowering: Early spring through summer; fruiting spring through fall.
best_field_traits: Fresh latex is pale/light yellow; A. aurantiaca is orange to reddish-orange.
Mature capsule prickles are mostly simple and much shorter; longest about 6–10(-12) mm.
Sepal horns are about 4–6(-10) mm and usually unarmed or only sparingly prickly near the base.

field_diagnostics.single_best_trait: Pale-yellow latex versus orange/reddish-orange latex in A. aurantiaca.

look_alikes.distinction: A. aurantiaca has orange/reddish-orange latex, longer prickly sepal horns, and much longer, often branched capsule prickles.
A. polyanthemos also has yellow latex but tends to have thicker/leathery, strongly glaucous leaves and differs in leaf division and sepal-horn characters.
